chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'Your Mawla, Ali ibn Mahziyar, bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf from an estate, a quarter of which is designated for you, for one Hajj each year, up to twenty Dinars. And that the road to Al-Basra was cut off, causing the expenses to double upon the people, so twenty Dinars are no longer sufficient. And several of your Mawali have bequeathed similarly regarding their Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Make three Hajjs count as two, God willing.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam adjust the financial requirements for Hajj when costs increased?
ai.summary: This correspondence from Imam al-Hadi (AS) to Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar illustrates the principle of *fiqh al-waqi'* (jurisprudence of context), where the Imam adjusts fixed bequests to account for inflation and disrupted trade routes to Basra. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical flexibility (*tawassul*) in fulfilling religious obligations, ensuring that the deceased's Hajj is completed despite economic shifts, rather than being limited by rigid literalism.
